author: The Linux Foundation
description:
Running massive AI training jobs, LLM inference workloads, and bursty AI agents on the same Kubernetes cluster is a recipe for wasted GPU capacity, fragmented resource allocation, and skyrocketing cloud costs. The problem isn't just deployment—it's intelligent scheduling that prevents idle resources while maintaining low-latency performance for unpredictable agent workloads.

Jesse Stutler, Maintainer at Volcano, explains how Volcano 1.14 is evolving from a batch scheduling tool into an AI-native unified scheduling platform. With its new multi-scheduler architecture, topology-aware scheduling, and KV cache awareness, Volcano handles the full AI lifecycle—training, inference, and agents—on a single cluster without sacrificing performance or burning through GPU budgets.

Key Topics Covered:
Multi-scheduler architecture with dynamic sharding for batch and agent workloads
Topology-aware scheduling for hyper-node bin packing and network domain optimization
AgentCube: Kubernetes-native plat
title: From Batch to AI-Native: How Volcano 1.14 Unifies Training, Inference & Agent Workloads

author: The Linux Foundation
description:
Bassam Tabbara, Maintainer of Crossplane, explains why manual infrastructure operations are becoming a liability as enterprises try to move faster with cloud-native and AI workloads. As organizations push for more automation, the gap between human-operated systems and machine-speed infrastructure is becoming impossible to ignore.
In this conversation, Tabbara discusses how Crossplane brings a declarative control model to cloud and AI infrastructure, why the project’s CNCF graduation matters, and how platform engineering teams are using control planes to manage increasingly complex environments across clouds and emerging AI workloads.
Key Topics Covered:
How Crossplane extends the Kubernetes-style declarative control model to cloud and AI infrastructure across providers.
Why platform engineering teams are using control planes to build internal developer platforms and reduce operational friction.
What Crossplane’s CNCF graduation says about ecosystem maturity, adoption, and enterprise-s
title: Crossplane Graduation and the Cost of Manual Cloud Ops | Bassam Tabbara, Crossplane
